Apple has released the fifth developer beta of iOS 27. iOS 27 beta 5 continues Apple's beta cycle this summer, with the official release expected next month. We'll install it on our devices right away and share anything new we discover.

Apple releases fifth iOS 27 developer beta for testing

The fifth developer beta is available for download on eligible iPhones via the Settings app. If you've signed up for the Apple Developer Program, you can go to Settings > General > Software Update > Beta Updates, then select iOS 27 Developer Beta.

The developer beta released today is expected to become public beta 3 of iOS 27. The official version for general users will launch next month.

As always, using beta software may still come with bugs, reduced battery life, app compatibility issues, and other hiccups.

iOS 27 focuses on Siri AI

iOS 27 can be said to be one of Apple's most AI-focused iPhone updates to date. The biggest change is Siri AI—a completely rebuilt assistant powered by the next generation of Apple Intelligence and brand-new Apple Foundation Models.

Siri AI delivers richer conversations, personalised content, broader world knowledge, on-screen content awareness, and deeper app actions across the system.

On iPhone, Siri AI also features a new visual experience that integrates with Dynamic Island, plus a dedicated Siri app that lets users review their conversation history across devices.

Visual Intelligence is also coming to Siri, including a new Siri mode within the Camera app and improvements to iPhone Camera Control.

Apple Intelligence is also expanding to more apps. iOS 27 brings AI-powered improvements to Photos, Safari, Passwords, Mail, Messages, Phone, Shortcuts, Home, and more. As we mentioned in our breakdown of Apple's new Foundation Models, some features will run on-device while others will use Private Cloud Compute.

More iOS 27 features and changes

Beyond Siri and Apple Intelligence, iOS 27 brings plenty of iPhone-specific changes. Apple has refined the Liquid Glass design introduced last year, including adding a new Liquid Glass transparency slider so you can adjust the look of the system interface to your liking.

In addition, performance has been improved across app launch speed, Photos loading, launching the Camera in Low Power Mode, AirDrop transfers, and switching between Wi-Fi and mobile data.

Other iPhone changes include: keyword and star rating support in Photos, customisable slideshow playback, smoother camera operation, continuous sending in Messages, dual-capture FaceTime, custom EQ for AirPods, new recovery options, easier Apple Pay card switching, and an AI-generated wallpaper creation feature.

We're installing iOS 27 beta 5 right now and will update you with anything noteworthy later. In the meantime, you can check out Apple's launch event lineup for a full look at everything new in iOS 27.

Found anything new in this iOS 27 beta 5 build? Let us know in the comments below!
